html:
The Xinca are an Indigenous people of southeastern Guatemala, in Santa Rosa, Jutiapa and Jalapa. Their languages are not Mayan and form a small family of their own.

In the 1400s they lived between the Maya kingdoms such as the K'iche' to the north, the Pipil along the Pacific coast and the Lenca to the east. Spanish forces under Pedro de Alvarado fought them in 1524. Under colonial rule they lost most of their land, and the Xinca languages are almost gone. Since the 1990s a revival has grown, and Xinca communities have led protests against a large silver mine on their land.
